C  JUDGMENT

The claimants, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Additional District & Sessions Court (Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal), Ariyalur (for short, the Tribunal below) in the award dated 26.2.2020 in M.C.O.P.No.109 of 2019, have filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Court (Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal), Ariyalur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The case of the claimants/appellants is as follows :
(i) The claimants are the parents and the elder minor sisters of the minor child Komagan, aged about 2 1/2 years.

On 15.7.2016, the minor child Komagan was standing opposite to a petty shop and at about 2 PM, the lorry, which was driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit the minor child resulting in sustaining grievous injuries and later he succumbed to the injuries.
A first information report came to be registered in Crime No.181 of 2016 on the file of T.Pazhur Police Station.
It was under those circumstances the claim petition came to be filed by the claimants before the Tribunal below.
(ii) The second respondent filed a counter to the claim petition.

and on appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence,
came to the conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry.

Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal below proceeded to fix the total compensation at Rs.2,35,000/- in the following manner :

sentences.text:
The appellants/claimants, not satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Tribunal below,
filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent.
Though the first respondent was served and his name printed in the cause list, he https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis does not appear either in person or through counsel.
4. This Court has carefully considered the submissions made on either side and perused the materials available on record.
This Court has also carefully gone through the award passed by the Tribunal below.

5. The main ground that was urged by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants is that the Tribunal below had fixed the lump sum compensation without adopting the multiplier method and in view of the same, separate compensation was not paid under the head 'loss of income'.
6.
This Court has been consistently holding that with regard to the deceased minor child, the compensation can be fixed between Rs.30,000 and Rs.60,000/- depending upon the facts of the case.
The Apex Court in the case of Meena Devi Vs. Nunu Chand Mahto [reported in 2023 (1) SCC 204] held that Rs.30,000/- can be fixed as the notional annual income for a minor child.

entities.text: Meena Devi Vs. Nunu Chand Mahto [reported in 2023 (1) SCC 204
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, the age of the minor child was about 12 years.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.

Considering the fact that the appellants 1 & 2 /claimants 1 & 2 have lost a male child, aged about 2 1/2 years and the fact that they also have two more minor girl children, this Court is inclined to fix the notional annual income of the deceased minor child in this case at Rs.35,000/-.
Taking into consideration the age of the minor child at the time of accident, 15 can be adopted as the multiplier.
Thus, under the head 'loss of income', a compensation of Rs.5,25,000/- (Rs.35,000/- X 15) is fixed.
8. The Tribunal below fixed a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of consortium'.
This Court is inclined to modify the same and fix the compensation under the head 'loss of love and affection' and grant Rs.40,000/- for each of the claimants.
Thus, the total compensation under this head is arrived at Rs.1,60,000/-.

9. In view of the above discussions, this Court is inclined to modify the impugned award passed by the Tribunal below and enhance the compensation as follows :
Amount Sl.No. Compensation awarded under the head (in Rs.)
1. Loss of income 5,25,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Gunasekaran vs Thamilselvan on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147307924/
3 2. Loss of estate 15,000/-
3. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
4. Loss of love and affection 1,60,000/-
Total 7,15,000/-
10.
Thus, the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal below at Rs.2,35,000/- is enhanced to Rs.7,15,000/-.

The second respondent - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.7,15,000/-, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.

Out of the said sum of Rs.7,15,000/-, the parents of the deceased minor child namely claimants 1 & 2/appellant 1 and 2 are entitled to Rs.2.5 lakhs each and claimants 3 and 4/ appellants 3 and 4 would be entitled to Rs.1,07,500/- each.
On such deposit, claimants 1 and 2/appellants 1 and 2 are permitted to withdraw their respective shares together with interest.
However, the shares of the minor children shall be kept in fixed deposit till the minors attain majority.
Claimants 1 and 2/appellants 1 and 2 are permitted to withdraw only the interest accrued thereon once in three months till the minors attain majority.
The other directions issued by the Tribunal below with regard to the mode of payment of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation remain unaltered.
11. The above civil miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed in the above terms.
No costs.
